title: ACadRust 0.6.5 release freshness, issue-state, strict-recovery, test-denominator, and loss-disposition audit
mode: Primary-source web research and existing-plan refinement
scope: Freshness-check the current ACadRust package/docs/Cargo manifest/changelog and issue states against the earlier provisional comparator screen.
Separate malformed DWG header bounds from object-record counts, allocations, and optional-object recovery.
Refine existing PAR-07/S8, parser-hardening, owner-closure, writer-disposition, test-denominator, and ACIS semantic-evidence gates without adding fixtures or routine peer jobs.

sources.project: ACadRust issue #123: object count and allocation bounds
sources.revision: Issue page reviewed 2026-10-20; report reproduces ACadRust 0.6.3; issue remains open; linked commit 53007f3 and maintainer request to re-check
sources.observed: The report describes object-data mutations that can yield a clamped but fabricated large vertex array with zero-filled reads, or an allocation request reported at roughly 12 TiB. The maintainer says some fixes were implemented but no public independent retest is recorded.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Peer-specific hardening lead only; do not copy its caps, byte offsets, or behavior as format requirements.

sources.project: ACadRust issue #134: AC1032 auxiliary-object strict-bounds regression
sources.revision: Issue page reviewed 2026-10-20; report concerns 0.6.4; issue remains open; linked commit 0e46236 and maintainer request for corpus retest
sources.observed: The report says 70 of 351 private AC1032 drawings that worked on 0.6.3 fail on MLeader-context or associative records in 0.6.4 after stricter record-size bounds. The linked change attempts bounded auxiliary-record preservation; no public corpus result confirms the fix.
sources.evidenceCeiling: A compatibility-versus-bounds tradeoff report for a peer. It does not justify relaxing libdxfrw bounds or a broad current-peer claim.

sources.revision: Issue page reviewed 2026-10-20; original reproduction names 0.6.3 and main ea68744; closed as completed on 2026-10-20 after commit 95a8c2f; current 0.6.5 changelog records the claimed resolution, but no independent public corpus retest is linked
sources.observed: The report covers raw-only custom-class records, group-430 color-book names, and table/block XDATA. The 0.6.4 changelog says named colors and table-record XDATA are preserved and unsupported custom records are reported. The issue was closed by its owner on 2026-10-20, but neither the issue nor release note publishes an independent retest of the private corpus or promises byte-preserving output for unsupported custom classes.
sources.evidenceCeiling: A closed peer issue confirms only its tracked resolution state, not full arbitrary-record fidelity or current-release qualification.

sources.project: ACadRust published crate, docs.rs package page, current manifest, changelog, and ACIS primitive API
sources.revision: Freshness correction reviewed 2026-10-20: docs.rs latest and raw Cargo.toml identify 0.6.5, published 2026-10-18; prior note that docs.rs displayed 0.6.4 was stale/incorrect
sources.observed: Published docs.rs, docs.rs latest, and raw Cargo.toml agree on acadrust 0.6.5, published 2026-10-18; the manifest identifies MPL-2.0 and dependencies including nom, flate2, and encoding_rs. Docs declare DXF/DWG R/W across AC1009-AC1032 but qualify variable entity availability, incomplete AC1009 DWG fidelity, and default promotion of R12-tagged documents to R13 output. Docs state CI covers stable Linux/Windows/macOS plus wasm builds and that tests requiring drawings absent from the repository are ignored. Changelog 0.6.5 claims malformed-header reporting, bounded auxiliary-record recovery, orphan exclusion from model space, ACIS color/body-history fixes, and regression fixtures. ACIS primitive docs describe builders that construct topology for listed primitives; this is structural API scope, not independent kernel validation.
sources.evidenceCeiling: The correction removes the false docs.rs version mismatch. Mutable main/latest claims still require an exact crate checksum, source commit, command, platform/features, ignored-test count, and file/entity denominator before a candidate comparison can be scored. Release notes and constructed topology do not independently verify fixes, arbitrary 3D B-rep validity, or named consumer acceptance.

sources.observed: The plan already contains a provisional ACadRust screen and independent owners for bounded parsing, object frames, graph closure, explicit loss, and evidence admission.
sources.evidenceCeiling: This update links peer failure shapes to existing implementation owners; it does not confirm an uncovered local defect or add a new feature claim.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07/S8: keep ACadRust SCREENED_NOT_ADMITTED until source, crate, tests, lineage, and exact route are pinned coherently
DWG hardening: separate checked header-section ranges from object-frame count/allocation bounds and distinguish strict error from safe bounded auxiliary-record recovery
Owner closure: distinguish null, resolved, and missing owners; do not silently manufacture model-space membership
Writer disposition: separately account for raw-only classes, color-book names, and table/block XDATA as preserved, explicitly refused, diagnosed omission, or silent loss
assessment.planImpact: Treat recent ACadRust issues as version-specific test-design evidence and record 0.6.5 release-note fixes separately from independently verified outcomes. Preserve bounded parsing, isolate only well-framed optional failures, prevent owner re-homing from inflating valid geometry, and score writer routes by per-record loss disposition. Account for ignored missing-drawing tests, explicit AC1009 caveats, and the distinction between ACIS topology construction and independent kernel semantics. No peer run or support promotion is justified.

method.kind: Read-only primary-source issue/documentation review; plan and receipt update
method.limitations: Issue reports, docs.rs latest, and repository documentation are mutable. The 0.6.3/0.6.4 issue reproductions predate published 0.6.5; release-note fixes were not built or independently retested here. Missing-drawing tests are documented as ignored, and their full denominator was not inspected or run. Private customer corpora were not accessed. No peer source or artifact was executed.
